name: Vlaamse Gebarentaal
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Vlaams GebarentaalCentrum (VGTC), research reports 2008-2026 listed at https://vgtc.be/onderzoek/publicaties/ (Vermeerbergen 2010 Woordvolgorde; Vermeerbergen & Van Herreweghe 2011 Negatie, Interrogatie; Heyerick et al. 2011 Meervoud; Heyerick et al. 2014 Classifiers; Huys 2010 orale component; Janssens & Wuytjens 2023 gesproken componenten; etc.)
sources.note: Publication list examined; all reports concern morphosyntax, mouthings or lexicography; none addresses prosody or stress.

sources.citation: Demey, Eline. 2005. Fonologie van de Vlaamse Gebarentaal: distinctiviteit & iconiciteit. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Gent. 552 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on VGT stress/prominence. Deel I is a featural phonology (handshape, thumb, hand-internal movement, unselected fingers, one-/two-handed signs, loan handshapes, orientation, location, setting/path movement, contact) in Van der Kooij's dependency model; Deel II treats iconicity. The only occurrences of 'stress' are quotations of Klima & Bellugi (1979) on ASL and Johnston (1989) on Auslan intensification (Deel II, 2.5); grep for klemtoon/beklemtoon/prosodie/accent/suprasegment found no statement about VGT word-level prominence.

sources.citation: Vermeerbergen, Myriam & Mieke Van Herreweghe (or Van Herreweghe & Vermeerbergen). 2015. Flemish Sign Language. In: Jepsen, J. B., De Clerck, G., Lutalo-Kiingi, S. & McGregor, W. (eds.), Sign Languages of the World: A Comparative Handbook. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton / Preston: Ishara Press.
